result.title: How Does Local Landscape Geometry Evolve in Language Model Pre-Training?
result.summary: The scale and expense of pre-training language models make efficient hyperparameter tuning essential, yet a principled guidance is still missing. In this work, we analyze language model pre-training dynamics from a local landscape geometry perspective. Our study reveals two distinct phases. In Phase I, sharpness of the local landscape is initially high, leading to instability and loss plateaus under large learning rates (LRs). The landscape shifts from sharp to flatter regions early in training. This dynamic explains the necessity of LR warmup and further suggests that larger peak LRs require proportionally longer warmup periods. In Phase II, the local landscape is governed by the gradient noise scale. Our theory identifies a depth flatness trade-off: high noise from smaller batches widens the loss basin, whereas reduced noise from larger batches deepens it. This theory motivates a dynamic batch-size (BS) scheduler that begins with a small BS and increases it late in training. Together, we provide a unified view of loss landscape evolution, which translates into actionable tuning strategies for large-scale pre-training.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作从局部损失景观几何角度分析语言模型预训练动态，划分出两个阶段：早期尖锐度从高转为平坦，解释 LR warmup 的必要性；后期景观由梯度噪声尺度主导，并据此提出先小后大的动态 batch-size 调度策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本预训练的优化理论研究，但其「尖锐→平坦两阶段」与噪声尺度—盆地深度权衡，可能为 LVR 中 latent 表示几何、推理期动态计算预算（何时投入更多/更少）与训练稳定性提供类比线索，可供核查。
